assertion_audit: tests/test_bank_step_speed.py:30 fails when toggling condition_diagnostics changes the computed update relative to the default branch; a common solver error can move both sides together, so this is a branch-parity check only.
tests/test_bank_step_speed.py:31 fails when the false branch returns a finite condition_before, but remains true if the two condition calculations execute and their values are discarded.
tests/test_bank_step_speed.py:32 fails when balancing does not reduce the synthetic matrix condition number; it measures the default branch and cannot establish the fast branch's cost.

evidence.baseline_suite_note: No baseline_suite object or baseline gate log was recorded by the reviewed run; the complete current-head after arm has zero failures, so added failures within its one-test scope are zero, but a paired baseline comparison is unavailable.

findings.text: The speed switch defaults to true and every checked runtime caller omits condition_diagnostics=False, so the shipped warm Newton path still computes both expensive condition estimates and no production path reaches the intended shortcut.
The only H200 whole-step profile times the default diagnostics path before the final change; no current-head H200 wall, device-time or launch receipt demonstrates the 0.5 ms and 100-launch limits.
The NaN output assertion remains green if the false branch computes both condition numbers and discards them, so it cannot fail on the performance regression the new switch claims to prevent.

The new trace parser duplicates GPU-event counting already owned by scripts/prototypes/sub_millisecond/parse_launch_trace.py:9-48 and counts every GPU X event rather than identifying kernel and host graph launches; disposition: folded into the next bank-step-speed repair node.
